transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I keep losing important papers and tools I need for jobs, and it’s starting to hurt my business. I work as a carpenter, and lately, keeping track of everything has just become overwhelming.
Did these attention and memory problems start after a specific stressful event or life change, or have you had them since childhood?

Looking back, I've actually struggled with things like daydreaming and losing school papers since I was a kid in elementary school. But it became completely unmanageable about a year and a half ago when my husband passed away. I had to take over all the administrative and scheduling work for my carpentry business, and I've been drowning in it ever since.
Before your husband passed away, did these attention and organization problems already cause major problems in work or daily life, or did they only become a real issue after that loss?

Before he passed, it never caused major problems in my work because my husband handled all of our scheduling, billing, and paperwork while I did the hands-on carpentry. I've always been a bit disorganized, but it only became a real, overwhelming issue once I had to take on all those administrative tasks myself.

When you were a child and teenager, did your daydreaming, losing things, or trouble staying organized also cause problems at school or at home, or was it mostly mild until your husband died and your responsibilities increased?

It definitely caused issues back then, too. I was always the kid who forgot to bring homework home, lost permission slips, and daydreamed through instructions. My teachers used to tell my parents that I was smart but just couldn't seem to pay attention or stay organized.
Did your attention and organization problems continue even during times when you were not grieving or under major stress, or did they mostly appear after your husband died?

Yes, those struggles have been with me my whole life, even during calm times when I wasn't grieving. I've always had a hard time keeping track of things and staying focused, but my husband managed the office so it didn't hurt my work. It's just that since he passed, I can't hide it or manage it anymore.

Before age 12, did you already have clear problems with inattention or disorganization at school or home, such as losing things, not finishing work, or being told you were daydreaming or not listening?

Yes, absolutely. Even back in elementary school, I was always forgetting to bring homework home, losing permission slips, and daydreamed through instructions. My teachers used to tell my parents that I was smart but just couldn't seem to pay attention or stay organized.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one setting, such as at work, at home, and in social situations, or only when you’re doing paperwork for the business?

It definitely happens in other places, not just when I'm doing paperwork. I'm constantly tearing my house and my truck apart looking for misplaced tools, keys, or checks I've set down. I also struggle to just sit still and relax, whether I'm waiting at the bank, in a client meeting, or even just trying to sit quietly on my porch.
Do you also often act on impulse, like interrupting people, blurting out answers, or making quick decisions you later regret?

No, I don't really struggle with acting on impulse, interrupting others, or making hasty decisions. My difficulties are much more about losing track of details, getting distracted, and feeling restless when I have to sit still.
Do you often feel unusually fidgety or unable to stay seated, or do you tend to interrupt people and act before thinking?

I definitely feel very restless and fidgety when I have to sit still, like I have an internal buzz and need to tap my feet or constantly fiddle with things. However, I don't really think I interrupt people or act before thinking. It is really just that physical restlessness that gets to me.
Do your restlessness and fidgeting ever lead you to leave your seat, wander around, or have trouble staying quietly in situations where you’re expected to sit still?

I don't necessarily get up and wander around in those situations, but I feel a strong restless buzz inside and constantly shift in my chair or tap my foot. I also have a lot of trouble just relaxing or staying quiet, and I quickly get fidgety and need to fiddle with something or talk to someone because I feel so antsy.
Have you ever had clear problems with impulsive behavior, such as interrupting people, blurting things out, making hasty decisions, or acting without thinking that caused trouble at work or at home?

No, I’ve never really had issues with impulsivity or acting without thinking. My struggles are much more about staying focused, keeping organized, and feeling physically restless and fidgety when I have to sit still.
Do your attention problems and restlessness make it hard for you to finish tasks, follow through on instructions, or stay organized in a way that causes problems at work or at home?

Yes, it's caused major problems for my carpentry business because I struggle to finish paperwork, constantly bouncing between half-finished contracts and invoices. I also make embarrassing mistakes on material orders and measurements, which has led to late billing, mixed-up job schedules, and very frustrated clients. I'm honestly terrified I won't be able to keep the business running, let alone start the women's mentoring workshop I've always dreamed of.
Have you had these same attention and restlessness problems since childhood, and were they more just inattention and fidgetiness rather than frequent impulsive behavior or acting out?

Yes, that's exactly right. Back in elementary school, I was always daydreaming, forgetting my homework, and losing permission slips rather than acting out or being impulsive. My teachers always told my parents that I was smart but just couldn't seem to pay attention or stay organized.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, with clear onset in childhood, symptoms present across settings, and current clinically significant occupational impairment. She confirms longstanding inattention/disorganization (daydreaming, losing papers, forgetting homework, difficulty finishing tasks) and associated restlessness/fidgetiness, but denies prominent impulsivity, interrupting, or acting without thinking. Symptoms were present before age 12 and persist into adulthood.
